A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NestQuant study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulated matrix-multiplication experiments, Llama benchmark evaluations, and appendix results covering runtime, ablations, and quantization settings.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations, Llama evaluations, runtime measurements, and appendix analyses reported in v2.

M1.justification: NestQuant’s nested-lattice quantizer, scaling-coefficient selection, QA-LDLQ, and NestQuantM remain unchanged, including their main-text and appendix algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic Gaussian matrix products, WikiText2, and the same five zero-shot benchmarks. Appendix evaluation tasks are unchanged; the added DuQuant result concerns existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The Llama-3-8B comparison now includes DuQuant at W4A4KV16, where v2 had no result; DuQuant already participated for Llama-2 models. Figure 1 also adds OSTQuant and QuaRot markers, largely redisplaying comparisons already present in Table 2.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same evaluation metrics, WikiText2 splits, 2048-token context, calibration procedures, and quantization configurations. The added DuQuant entry uses the existing W4A4KV16 comparison setting.

E4.justification: The noise-amplification analysis, scaling-strategy comparison, LDLQ and rotation ablations, and sensitivity to the number of scaling coefficients are unchanged. All appendix pages are identical.

E5.justification: No repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised. The existing point-estimate reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the missing DuQuant Llama-3-8B W4A4KV16 entry with WikiText2 perplexity 8.06, also plotted in Figure 1. The newly plotted OSTQuant weight-only marker is approximately 6.35, inconsistent with Table 2’s unchanged 6.53. NestQuant’s results and all appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemma 4.2 and its proof, Lemma D.1 and its proof, and the dynamic-programming derivation in Appendix F are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about a general quantized-matrix-product primitive, its application to LLMs, and its performance advantages. The added comparisons do not revise these claims’ scope.

C2.justification: The shaping-gain explanation, noise-amplification and bias tradeoff, computational-cost discussion, and scaling-coefficient tradeoff remain unchanged. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, CUDA listings, hardware information, calibration instructions, and scaling-coefficient details are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment provides no new implementation or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 35 references and research positioning. DuQuant, OSTQuant, and QuaRot were already cited and included among comparison methods.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Air Force funding acknowledgment and associated disclaimer on page 11 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds four comparator entries, expands and rearranges the legend, changes marker symbols, and revises the y-axis range and ticks. Other figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The DuQuant 8.06 entry fills a missing comparison, and Figure 1 presents more baselines together. However, its new OSTQuant weight-only marker conflicts with Table 2, introducing numerical inconsistency into the overview plot. These limited completeness and presentation gains coexist with a reporting defect, while the method, theory, and remaining evidence are unchanged; a net quality improvement is unclear.
